sourceItems.title: Rising Costs to Drive Further Increases in EV Cell Prices in 2Q26
normalizedClaims: ESS cell prices were stable with strong demand, full order books and high utilization; 2Q26 demand was expected to remain solid while raw-material costs pushed cell pricing upward.

sourceItems.title: GE Vernova Releases First Quarter 2026 Financial Results
normalizedClaims: Orders were $18.3B, +71% organically; backlog rose $13B sequentially; Electrification booked $2.4B of data-center equipment orders in Q1, more than all of 2025; 2026 guidance was raised.

sourceItems.title: ABB Q1 2026 results
normalizedClaims: Group orders rose 32% and comparable orders 24%; Electrification comparable orders rose 44%, order backlog rose 40%, and data-center orders grew triple-digits.

sourceItems.title: Strong AI Demand vs. Weak Consumer Segment Creates Pricing Divergence Among MLCC Suppliers
normalizedClaims: AI demand remained strong while consumer demand was soft; rising silver, aluminum and copper costs drove 10-15% average price increases in several passive components from April 1; OEMs were building inventory amid component tightness.

sourceItems.title: 2026年4月中国采购经理指数运行情况
normalizedClaims: April manufacturing PMI was 50.3; production 51.5 and new orders 50.6 remained expansionary while supplier delivery time stayed below 50.

sourceItems.title: 2026年4月份工业生产者出厂价格同比上涨2.8% 环比上涨1.7%
normalizedClaims: April PPI rose 2.8% YoY and 1.7% MoM; purchasing prices rose 3.5% YoY and 2.1% MoM; non-ferrous materials/wires rose 21.3% YoY and chemical raw materials 5.9%.

sourceItems.title: Server DIMM Price May 2026
normalizedClaims: Server DRAM contract prices kept rising because of supply deficits and depleted inventories; cloud/server demand remained robust and the market undersupplied.

sourceItems.title: Agentic AI Drives Structural Expansion in Memory Demand
normalizedClaims: TrendForce sharply raised its 2026 and 2027 global memory-market forecasts and said the supply deficit was unlikely to resolve in the short term as inference-centric AI expanded memory demand.

sourceItems.title: 2026年5月中国采购经理指数运行情况
normalizedClaims: May manufacturing PMI fell to 50.0; new orders were 49.9 and new export orders 48.6, while production remained 51.2; raw-material purchasing-price index stayed high at 60.5.

sourceItems.title: China factory activity stalls in May as demand weakens
normalizedClaims: Reuters highlighted May PMI at 50.0, weaker new/export orders and continuing raw-material cost pressure.

sourceItems.title: Rapid Contract Price Surge Drives 1Q26 DRAM Industry Up 81% QoQ
normalizedClaims: 1Q26 conventional DRAM contract prices rose roughly 93-98% QoQ and industry revenue rose 81% QoQ to $97B; supplier inventories remained extremely low in Q2.

sourceItems.title: 2026年5月份工业生产者出厂价格同比上涨3.9% 环比上涨0.5%
normalizedClaims: May PPI rose 3.9% YoY; producer purchasing prices rose 5.8% YoY; non-ferrous materials/wires rose 22.0%, chemicals 11.8% and fuel/power 10.0%.

sourceItems.title: Contract Prices Surged More Than 100% in 1H26; Structural Shortages to Keep NOR Flash and SLC NAND Prices Rising in 2H26
normalizedClaims: NOR Flash and SLC NAND contract prices rose more than 100% cumulatively in 1H26 as capacity shifted to higher-value memory; no significant capacity expansion was visible and shortages were expected to continue.

sourceItems.title: G7 sets up critical minerals alliance, platform to cut reliance on China
normalizedClaims: G7 governments created a critical-minerals alliance/crisis platform and discussed stockpiling, subsidies and procurement to reduce single-source dependence.
observedChanges: policy response to supply-chain concentration intensifies

sourceItems.title: Hormuz half-open: tanker fleet prices in recovery hope
normalizedClaims: By late June tanker operators were repositioning for recovery in Gulf exports; VLCC earnings had fallen sharply as vessels crowded the Middle East even though physical flows were not fully normalized.

eventClusters.statement: Memory tightness moved from a cyclical price-upgrade story toward a broader structural shortage in Q2: realized DRAM revenue and prices surged, inventories stayed very low, and mature NOR/SLC supply was squeezed by capacity migration.
eventClusters.contradictionSearchNotes: All Q2 discovery items share one specialist origin. Deep research must independently verify A-share company realization and test whether the enormous Q1/Q2 re-rating already absorbed the reset.
eventClusters.researchQuestion: Did any A-share memory company show a newly realized earnings reset that still had price-relative room versus peers at a Q2 cutoff?

eventClusters.statement: Global electrification/power-equipment demand accelerated beyond the already-strong Q4/Q1 narrative: GE Vernova and ABB independently reported record/rapid order growth, sharp backlog expansion and unusually strong data-center electrification demand.
eventClusters.contradictionSearchNotes: The theme was already known. V0.7 must require a new A-share company-level acceleration/baseline reset rather than recycling prior thematic winners.
eventClusters.researchQuestion: Did a specific A-share supplier report an acceleration or guidance reset large enough to create a fresh cross-sectional edge?

eventClusters.statement: Energy-storage cells entered Q2 with strong demand, full order books and high utilization while raw-material costs pushed battery-cell pricing from flat toward an upward bias.
eventClusters.contradictionSearchNotes: EV demand remained weaker and higher lithium/copper/aluminum costs can reduce cell-maker margin. One specialist origin requires first-party company confirmation.
eventClusters.researchQuestion: Which A-share battery maker, if any, converts ESS utilization into accelerating profit rather than just revenue while preserving margins?

eventClusters.statement: AI infrastructure demand and strategic inventory building supported passive components while consumer demand stayed soft; simultaneously silver/aluminum/copper inflation triggered broad 10-15% passive-component price increases.
eventClusters.contradictionSearchNotes: Price hikes may only offset metal cost inflation; consumer weakness may overwhelm AI mix benefits. Deep research must separate pass-through from real margin expansion.
eventClusters.researchQuestion: Is there an A-share passive-component supplier with verified AI mix acceleration and pricing power beyond simple cost pass-through?

eventClusters.statement: China producer/input inflation accelerated sharply in April-May, especially in non-ferrous metals, chemicals and fuel/power.
eventClusters.contradictionSearchNotes: Broad input inflation identifies cost pressure but not who captures margin; downstream demand weakened in May.
eventClusters.researchQuestion: Does this broad signal contain any narrow, independently verified earnings mechanism or should it remain macro context?

eventClusters.statement: China manufacturing demand softened by May: PMI fell to 50.0, new orders slipped below 50 and export orders weakened even as production remained expansionary and input-price pressure stayed high.
eventClusters.contradictionSearchNotes: Reuters is derivative of the official NBS release and does not create an independent origin. Broad weakness can be context but lacks a specific beneficiary.
eventClusters.researchQuestion: Is this only a macro contradiction filter for other Q2 themes?

eventClusters.statement: Governments escalated strategic responses to concentrated critical-mineral supply chains, including a G7 alliance/crisis platform and prospective stockpiling/investment measures.
eventClusters.contradictionSearchNotes: Policy intent is not the same as realized shortage, price or company earnings. A single policy report is insufficient for selection.
eventClusters.researchQuestion: Is there a pre-cutoff realized physical/economic change behind the policy response, or only strategic narrative?

eventClusters.statement: The Q1 Hormuz tanker-rate shock began reversing by late Q2 as fleets repositioned for export recovery; VLCC earnings fell sharply even before physical flows fully normalized.
eventClusters.contradictionSearchNotes: This directly challenges extrapolating the Q1 spot-rate spike. It is a negative-control/reversal event, not a reason to preserve a stale long thesis.
eventClusters.researchQuestion: Does the system correctly retire short-half-life shipping shocks when physical/rate evidence reverses?
